subject: Private deployment pen-test — network baseline, egress IPs, and remediation ETA
messages:
From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@fintechco.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintechco.com, samir.patel@fintechco.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pen-test evidence & boundary assumptions for private deployment

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our vendor risk review we need additional detail from your penetration test and a short explanation of the network/host boundary assumptions for Redwood Private when deployed into a customer VPC. Specifically we need:

- The pen-test report (redacted is fine) that covers the private deployment topology, not just the hosted API.
- A CSV or list of egress IPs/NAT IP ranges we should allow in our outbound firewall rules.
- Clarification whether any Redwood-managed agents/example containers receive inbound connections from the public internet in our VPC, or if all inbound is customer-initiated.
- How credentials (API keys, TLS certs) are handled in the private deployment (are any long-lived credentials stored on hosts in our subnets?).
- Current remediation status and ETA for any open high/critical findings discovered during the last engagement.

We have an internal deadline to close the assessment by Feb 20th, so a response this week would be ideal. If you prefer we can use the CAIQ/SIG matrix but the items above are priority.

Thanks,
Lina Ortiz
Head of Vendor Risk — FinTechCo

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@fintechco.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen-test evidence & boundary assumptions for private deployment

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Looping in our security lead Mina (cc) and Solutions engineer Marissa so they can provide the report and a short summary of boundary/egress behavior for Private deployments.

Quick answers while they pull attachments:
- We can provide a redacted pen-test summary focused on Private (you'll see the PDF attached in our internal follow-up).
- We will include a CSV of egress IPs used by control-plane connectors and transient NAT addresses for the current release. Note: some customers use NAT gateways they control; we provide the control-plane IP ranges for outbound allowlists.
- Redwood Private is deployed so that customer workloads and data live in your VPC. Our control-plane connectors make outbound TLS-only connections to Redwood; we do not require inbound public access into your private subnets.
- Long-lived keys are not stored in plaintext on customer hosts. Host agents use short-lived mTLS certificates and/or instance profile credentials where supported; we'll detail rotation periods in the attached summary.

Mina — can you attach the pen-test summary and add the current remediation ETA for the three outstanding items we discussed? Marissa/ I will coordinate a short call with FinTechCo if needed.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0194

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@fintechco.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen-test evidence & boundary assumptions for private deployment — report and remediation status

Hi Lina/Team,

Attached: 1) 202601-Redwood-private-pen-test-summary.pdf (redacted executive summary + findings) 2) pen-test-evidence-archive-202601.zip (screenshots, logs, PoCs redacted) 3) private-deploy-egress-ips.csv (current outbound IPs)

Executive summary (high level):
- Scope: internal review and third-party engagement against our Private deployment reference (customer VPC + Redwood control-plane connectors). Testing targeted network egress controls, host hardening, credential handling, and API authentication flows.
- Key findings (all classified and tracked):
  - HIGH: outdated host agent package on a pre-release build (affects agent < 2.3.1). Patch available; rollout in progress.
  - MEDIUM: weak default WAF rule set for a legacy management endpoint exposed to control-plane testing — mitigated via rule update.
  - LOW: telemetry upload endpoint accepted additional headers; low-risk.

Boundary assumptions (how Redwood Private sits relative to customer VPC):
- Deployment model: Redwood Private installs a small control-plane connector and optional host agent into customer-managed subnets within your VPC. Customer retains network control — we do not provision public-facing load balancers inside your private subnets unless mutually agreed.
- Inbound vs outbound: All Redwood-initiated network traffic from connectors to Redwood control plane is outbound TLS (HTTPS) on port 443. There are no inbound public IPv4 endpoints provisioned by Redwood into customer private subnets in the default configuration.
- Egress IPs: The attached CSV lists current control-plane egress IPs and short description (these are IPs used by Redwood-managed control-plane endpoints). If you use your own NAT gateway the actual source IPs will be your NAT addresses; allowlisting at your perimeter should include the CSV list for direct allowlists where customers do not NAT. Sample IPs (for quick reference): 52.204.12.77, 18.205.92.10, 54.153.22.5.
- Credential handling:
  - Host agents obtain short-lived mTLS certs from Redwood CA with a default TTL of 4 hours. Private keys are stored in a process-isolated agent runtime and rotated automatically; persistent long-lived secrets are not stored in plaintext on customer hosts.
  - Control-plane authentication uses mutual TLS + token-based auth; tokens are scoped and have short TTLs.

Remediation status & ETA (open items):
- Agent patch (HIGH): rollout to customer images started 2026-02-11; target 100% of active Private deployments by 2026-02-18.
- WAF rule hardening (MEDIUM): rules updated on 2026-02-10; residual tuning through 2026-02-16.
- Regression test & verification: scheduled internal re-test 2026-02-17; we will share verification logs and a short test summary.

Planned deliverables this week: redacted pen-test summary PDF + evidence archive + CSV with egress IPs (attached). After re-test we will provide a short verification memo. If FinTechCo requires, we can schedule a scoped follow-up penetration test between Feb 22–26 (engineer time) for a nominal fee.

Notes & caveats:
- Egress ranges are for our control-plane endpoints and may change between releases; we recommend allowlisting by DNS + IP ranges and agreeing a window for changes.
- For highly regulated customers we recommend Private + VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) patterns to completely avoid public egress from your subnets; we can scope that in a design call.

Attachments referenced: 202601-Redwood-private-pen-test-summary.pdf (4 pages redacted), private-deploy-egress-ips.csv (1 file), pen-test-evidence-archive-202601.zip (contains redacted artifacts).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen-test evidence & boundary assumptions for private deployment — quick follow-up

Thanks Mina and Connor — the materials are helpful and the CSV of egress IPs is exactly what our infra team needed. Two quick follow-ups before we close:

- Can you confirm audit log retention for the agent telemetry and whether those logs (redacted) can be made available for a 3rd-party audit? We need at least 90 days of retention for event logs tied to configuration changes.
- Please share the verification memo after your re-test (ideally the week of Feb 17). If the high finding patch lands by Feb 18 and verification is complete, FinTechCo will consider the item closed.

If these are straightforward we should be able to finish our assessment by Feb 20. Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Lina
Head of Vendor Risk — FinTechCo
